Sobota, Inna Vishik, Shuolong Yang, Ming Yi, Timothy Zaklama

articles.title: Valley-resolved high harmonics probe symmetry breaking beyond the Dirac cone
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.15251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-energy electrons in graphene obey an emergent, rotationally invariant Dirac equation, while the honeycomb lattice enters only through higher-order, symmetry-breaking corrections, the leading one being trigonal warping. This provides a unique solid-state arena to address a cornerstone challenge in quantum gravity: how to detect ultraviolet symmetry-breaking granular corrections, suppressed by a fundamental scale, atop an emergent infrared relativistic continuum. We show that intense counter-rotating ømega-2ømega fields and valley-resolved high-harmonic generation (HHG) provide such a probe. Within a family of models that interpolates continuously between the isotropic Dirac cone and nearest-neighbour graphene at fixed Fermi velocity, the valley contrast of the harmonic yield vanishes identically in the symmetric theory, grows linearly with the warping coupling, and its valley-even counterpart appears only at second order, as expected from effective-field-theory power counting. The stronger the laser, the farther it drives electrons from the Dirac points, so the laser intensity plays the role of the collision energy. For the fourth harmonic, the leading warping correction alone accounts for the valley contrast of real graphene up to fundamental intensities of about 10¹¹ W/cm², below the damage threshold of monolayer graphene, whereas the fifth harmonic already reveals higher-order lattice corrections at intensities around 10¹⁰ W/cm². The two harmonics, which rotate in opposite directions, are emitted by opposite valleys. Valley-resolved harmonics are far more sensitive than the residual valley populations, making them a practical detector of lattice-scale physics hidden beneath an emergent Dirac theory.
authors: Pablo Pais, Alfredo Iorio, Marcelo F. Ciappina

articles.title: Field Response of the Orbital Moment Probed by Integrated Magnetic Circular Dichroism
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.15684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) is an optical probe of orbital time reversal symmetry breaking. Although frequency integrated MCD is related to the self-rotation contribution to orbital magnetization at zero field, its magnetic response generally differs from the thermodynamic orbital susceptibility. Here, we define the MCD susceptibility and derive general expressions for multiband systems using an electromagnetic U(1) gauge invariant approach. For insulators, the response contains contributions from the non-Abelian quantum metric, Berry curvature, and field induced interband mixing. For metals, a finite temperature Green function formulation separates the smooth response into Fermi sea and Fermi surface contributions. An independent Landau level calculation confirms the expressions for the zero-field MCD moment and its linear magnetic response. In a continuum model for twisted bilayer graphene, the MCD susceptibility vanishes within the charge neutrality gap, while the thermodynamic orbital susceptibility remains markedly diamagnetic. Near the gap edges, the orbital moment term dominates the response. Features near the van Hove energies are associated with density of states enhancement. These results clarify how the two susceptibilities reflect different orbital processes even for the same electronic structure and thus establish the MCD susceptibility as a distinct probe of orbital magnetic response.
authors: Qian-Sheng Shi, Ziqiang Wang, Jian Kang, Yi Zhang

articles.title: Approaching Irrational Quantization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.15753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integer and fractional quantum Hall effects reveal that quantized physical responses can take integer and fractional values, respectively. This naturally raises the question of whether quantization can extend beyond rational numbers to an irrational value. Here we show that such a quantized response can emerge from the limiting behavior of a finite, experimentally realizable geometric network. We develop a method based on infinite geometric structures, in which a sequence of finite networks rapidly converges toward an infinite limit. Following this approach, we identify a planar network whose normalized resistance converges to the irrational value sqrt3, and realize a finite approximation with high-precision geometric control. The measured normalized resistance is 1.735 ± 0.001, h/e² for a fully occupied Landau level in the designed pattern. Our experimental results extend the concept of quantization beyond rational values and demonstrate that an irrational quantized response can be approached through a finite physical system.
authors: Zhihong Wu, Zhimou Chen, Siyuan Zhang, Jinyang Chen, L. N. Pfeiffer, K. W. West, Yang Liu, Xi Lin

articles.title: Nonrelativistic Optically-Induced Spin Torque in Noncollinear Magnets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Manipulating spin using contactless and non-invasive optical approaches is one of the forefront topic in the modern spintronic science and technology. Prior studies on optically-induced spin reorientation usually scales with spin-orbit coupling strength, setting a limitation on composing heavy elements. In this work, we extend such a limit into nonrelativistic regime by exploring noncollinear magnetic configuration. Using a general spin group-theoretical investigation, we show how the symmetric operators in both spin and lattice spaces control the spin torque and quantum geometry of Bloch wavefunction--including both quantum metric and Berry curvature. We describe their site-resolved spin symmetries and unravel their selection rules. Furthermore, we adopt a Kagomé lattice model and a realistic material family to showcase the local spin torque under light irradiation. Since the nonrelativistic spin splitting usually spans on the order of electron-volt, significantly larger than typical spin-orbit induced splitting, the nonrelativistic light-induced spin torque is concomitantly much stronger. This work extends the previous opto-spintronics from relativistic to nonrelativistic limit, significantly broadening its realization platform.
authors: Zhiyuan Li, Jian Zhou

articles.title: High-mobility spin transport mediated by indirect excitons in a van der Waals heterostructure
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient spin transport with high spin mobility is of both fundamental and practical significance for spintronics. Spin can be transferred by moving particles. However, particle scattering limits spin transfer and prevents high spin mobilities. In this work, we study the kinetics of spin transport mediated by a quantum system of indirect excitons (IXs) in a van der Waals heterostructure composed of atomically thin transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs). This spin transfer mechanism allows for the realization of efficient spin transport characterized by a high spin mobility reaching 10⁵ cm²/(eVḑots), which is orders of magnitude higher than that achieved via standard diffusive spin transport in TMD materials. The suppression of IX scattering enables high-mobility spin transport.
authors: Zhiwen Zhou, W. J. Brunner, Luc M. Nguyen, C. A. Lozano, G. Mercado, L. H. Fowler-Gerace, L. V. Butov

articles.title: Self-Avoidance Governs Re-entrant Coil-Globule Transition of Inertial Active Brownian Ring Polymers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16188v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Active matter systems composed of self-propelled entities exhibit a wide range of out-of-equilibrium phase behaviors and collective dynamics. Assemblies of active particles, e.g., in a linear structure, are particularly interesting, as they exhibit an intriguing interplay between activity and geometrical restrictions due to self-avoidance and entanglements. Using Langevin dynamics simulations of an active Brownian ring polymer with translational and rotational inertia, we uncover an inertia-driven re-entrant coil-globule transition in the absence of any attractive interactions. We show that rotational inertia plays a paramount role, leading, in the globular state, to spontaneous, nonzero, radially outward polarization of the active forces. Self-avoidance and entanglements break the rotational symmetry of active beads and effectively stabilize the globular states. The transition becomes increasingly sharp with increasing rotational inertia, yielding highly compact globular conformations at intermediate activities, whereas at high activity the polymer re-expands into a coil state. Scaling of the radius of gyration reveals crossovers from self-avoiding, phantom-like to compact-globular structures. Further, rotational inertia enhances transport properties, with an intermediate activity-induced Rouse-type bead diffusion and a long-time diffusion coefficient displaying a power-law dependence on the moment of inertia. Our study establishes a purely inertia-induced mechanism for controlling the collapse of active polymers, arising from spontaneous active-force polarization and self-avoidance.
authors: Rakesh Palariya, Arindam Panda, Roland G. Winkler, Sunil P Singh

articles.title: Thermally Enhanced Pseudo-Goldstone Spin Gap in the Isotropic Helimagnet ZnCr₂Se₄
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In magnetically ordered systems, the spin gap in the magnon spectrum is normally expected to decrease on warming and close at the transition out of the long-range order. The presence of a pseudo-Goldstone gap is commonly associated with nonlinear terms in spin-wave theory. However, its precise origin and detailed properties can vary and remain under debate. Here we show by means of inelastic neutron scattering that the pseudo-Goldstone gap in the Heisenberg helimagnet ZnCr₂Se₄ exhibits an atypical, nonmonotonic temperature dependence: the gap increases over much of the ordered phase before closing near T_N. These results align with recent spin-dynamic simulations based on an effective quartic potential in an isotropic system~[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220411 (2026)]. As the pseudo-Goldstone spin gap in ZnCr₂Se₄ is dominated by quantum effects at subkelvin temperatures, its characteristic growth on warming is caused by thermal fluctuations.
authors: N. D. Andriushin, A. Sanders, J. Reuther, D. C. Peets, P. Steffens, A. Hiess, J. Lass, L. Prodan, V. Tsurkan, V. Felea, D. S. Inosov

articles.title: Photon echo from Maki-Thompson interference in a fluctuating s-wave superconductor
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study theoretically the nonlinear optical response of a fluctuating s-wave superconductor driven by two successive terahertz pulses. We show that the response exhibits a photon echo signal that arises from the quantum interference between the time-reversed electron and hole trajectories in the Maki-Thompson process. By contrast, the transport of the fluctuating Cooper pairs responsible for the Aslamazov-Larkin conductivity does not generate an echo. The photon echo signal can be readily measured using terahertz two-dimensional coherent spectroscopy, highlighting its potential to distinguish different fluctuation conductivity mechanisms.
authors: Hui Zhou, Yuan Wan

articles.title: Molecule-intercalated van der Waals Josephson junctions uncover complex multiband superconductivity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intercalation of molecular species provides a route to tailor the electronic structure in van der Waals superconductors, yet intercalated compounds have rarely been integrated into phase-sensitive quantum devices. Here, we realize hybrid molecular Josephson junctions based on TaS2/NbSe2 heterostructures. Selective intercalation of the TaS2 electrode induces monolayer-like Ising superconductivity, while the junctions exhibit asymmetric Fraunhofer interference, field-induced and spontaneous Josephson diode effects. The zero-field diode disappears upon reversing the electrode stacking and re-emerges after intercalating the lower NbSe2 electrode. These findings indicate that the hybrid superconducting electrode hosts unconventional superconductivity underlying the nonreciprocal transport, while molecular intercalation acts as a tuning knob for its internal phase structure. This behavior is consistent with a time-reversal-symmetry-breaking multiband superconducting state characterized by a nontrivial relative phase between superconducting condensates. Our results establish hybrid molecular Josephson junctions as a quantum-device platform for phase-sensitive investigation and integration of molecularly engineered superconductors, opening opportunities to uncover and engineer unconventional superconducting phases.
authors: Daniel Margineda, David Caldevilla-Asenjo, Covadonga Álvarez-García, Daniel Tezze, Raul Arenal, Maxim Ilyn, Celia Rogero, Luis E. Hueso, Marco Gobbi

articles.title: Probing quantum nonlinear phononics in multilayer graphene with time-resolved Raman scattering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coherently driven phonons are conventionally described classically. Nonlinear phonon-phonon interactions, however, allow an infrared drive to reshape the fluctuation spectrum and generate substantial nonthermal enhancement of phonon fluctuations, motivating a description beyond the coherent displacement alone. We benchmark classical and semiclassical approximations against the full quantum theory and find that the semiclassical treatment substantially improves agreement with the quantum dynamics. We propose nonequilibrium spontaneous Raman scattering as a sensitive probe of these effects and apply our framework to recent experiments suggesting quantum nonlinear phononics involving the E₁ᵤ and E₂g modes in multilayer graphene. At very strong pump fields, driving the E₁ᵤ mode significantly modifies the E₂g Raman spectrum; however, reproducing the reported response at experimental field strengths requires accounting for pump-induced Raman matrix element dynamics or alternative energy pathways into the E₂g mode. Our findings extend nonlinear phononics beyond average atomic displacements to the dynamics of lattice fluctuations, highlighting the interplay between coherent motion and quantum correlations in driven materials.
authors: Jakob Dolgner, Michael Rübhausen, Dirk Manske

articles.title: Admittance extraction of quantum dot arrays for charge sensing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work demonstrates admittance extraction of quantum dot arrays using a rate equation frame- work matching experimental reflectometry measurements. Using a semiclassical rate equation, we consider a perturbation of the source/drain chemical potential to model reflectometry readout in a quantum dot array. This is a time-dependent extension of the rate equation which has been employed in literature for pumped arrays of quantum dots and capacitance extractions. Here we extend this to a double quantum dot for admittance extraction. The simulations are calibrated us- ing Fermi-Hubbard parameters extracted from experimental data, which it is then shown to closely approximate to.
authors: Conor Power, Mathieu Moras, Andrii Sokolov, Robert Bogdan Staszewski, Elena Blokhina

articles.title: Emergent low-energy thermodynamics and universal B/T scaling in α-RuCl₃
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum spin liquids are exotic states of matter in which strongly interacting spins remain disordered down to zero temperature and host fractionalized excitations. This has motivated an extensive search for their realization in materials. Among candidate systems, α-RuCl₃ has drawn particular attention as a platform for the quantum spin liquid proposed by Kitaev, in which the low-energy excitations in applied magnetic fields are interpreted as itinerant Majorana fermions and local flux excitations. However, conflicting experimental signatures have cast doubt on whether a Kitaev quantum spin liquid-like state is really the right starting point to interpret the low-energy states in α-RuCl₃, motivating a closer look at the nature of these excitations. Here we report an extensive high field study of specific heat up to 35 T on α-RuCl₃. We find that the low-energy thermodynamics exhibit universal B/T scaling with a single effective energy scale proportional to the applied field as long as the magnetic field is not close to the c-axis. This behavior persists continuously from the antiferromagnetic phase boundary to the highest fields, suggesting that the perturbative Kitaev limit, with its Majorana and flux excitations, may not be an appropriate starting point for describing the low-energy thermodynamics of α-RuCl₃ for fields away from the c-axis.
authors: A. Khansili, B. J. Ramshaw, A. Bangura, H. -Y. Kee, R. D. McDonald, F. Assaad, A. Rydh, A. Shekhter, K. A. Modic

articles.title: Quantum skyrmion molecule: two quantum skyrmions bound by coherent magnon exchange
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.17299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum skyrmions in frustrated spin-1/2 magnets are bound states of a few flipped spins in a ferromagnetic background. Using exact diagonalization and density-matrix renormalization group calculations for the J₁₋₋J₂ triangular-lattice model with easy-axis anisotropy K, we ask what happens when two such objects are brought together. The binding energy per flipped spin of a single skyrmion has a minimum at Nf*=7 for K=0.02--0.04, and skyrmions smaller than Nf* do not exist as pairs: at any distance they coalesce into a single larger object, and pinning wells cannot prevent it. Two skyrmions of natural size, by contrast, form a bound molecule without pinning or external field, with binding energy Usimeq-0.007J₁ at K=0.03--0.04 and an equilibrium separation of 5.5 lattice spacings that does not depend on K or on the size of the simulation domain; at K=0.02, where the single skyrmion is itself marginally bound, the pair is unbound within our resolution. The two constituents keep their identity (7+7 flipped spins) and are coupled by a coherent exchange of magnons, visible as number fluctuations between the two halves of the domain in excess of those of two independent skyrmions and as in-plane spin correlations between the two skyrmion walls that reach 0.16 across the gap. These correlations follow the vortex pattern of the two textures and lock their relative helicity, the quantum counterpart of the helicity-dependent interaction of classical skyrmions. We discuss the molecule as a self-assembled two-qubit element for skyrmion helicity qubits in a single layer.
authors: Ricardo L. Silva

articles.title: Crystal growth, magnetic, and transport properties of the candidate altermagnet Cr₁/₄NbS₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.17452v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Altermagnetism is a rapidly emerging paradigm in condensed matter magnetism, yet the number of experimentally confirmed altermagnetic candidates remains remarkably limited. Cr₁/₄NbS₂ has long been theoretically proposed as a promising altermagnet, but there are no reports on experimental investigation of single crystals. Here, we report the successful growth of high-quality single crystals of Cr₁/₄NbS₂ and present its structural, thermal, magnetic, and transport properties. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction provides detailed crystallographic information and confirms the hexagonal crystal symmetry (P6₃/mmc), one of the criteria for altermagnetic behavior. Resistivity and heat capacity measurements unambiguously identify an antiferromagnetic Néel temperature of T_N sim 141 K. Magnetotransport measurements reveal non-trivial features in the magnetoresistance and Hall response, indicative of quantum diffusive transport phenomena. Cr₁/₄NbS₂, synthesized here for the first time in single-crystalline form, therefore serves as an experimental platform for probing the rich spectrum of phenomena predicted for altermagnetic materials.
authors: Nashra Pistawala, Martin R. Lees, Geetha Balakrishnan, Daniel A. Mayoh

articles.title: Electric Edelstein Effect in Two Dimensions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.17535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose the electric Edelstein effect (EEE) in two-dimensional (2D) systems, where crossed out-of-plane and in-plane electric fields generate a spin polarization. The gate field converts the Edelstein response from a material-fixed spin polarization into a gate-tunable one. A symmetry analysis over all magnetic layer point groups shows that the EEE is allowed in a wide range of magnetic and nonmagnetic systems, including ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, and altermagnets. The EEE plays two distinct roles: it generates spin polarization where the linear Edelstein effect (EE) is symmetry-forbidden, as in centrosymmetric materials; and it adds a new gate-tunable component, generally non-collinear with the conventional one, where the EE is already present. The two fields then act as independent knobs and raise the control dimension of the spin polarization from one to two. Our microscopic theory traces the EEE to band-geometric quantities, which are strongly enhanced near small band gaps. First-principles calculations predict pronounced effects in the centrosymmetric ferromagnet MnSe2, where the linear EE is symmetry-forbidden. In the nonmagnet SnSe where the EE and EEE coexist, the two knobs cover an extended region of the spin sphere. Our findings establish the EEE as a symmetry-guided, gate-tunable route to electrical spin manipulation and open avenues for multistate spintronics in 2D quantum materials.
authors: Xiaoran Lv, Tianqi Zhang, Chaoxi Cui, Yaling Li, Yi Shen, Weikang Wu, Ziming Zhu, Yugui Yao, Zhi-Ming Yu

articles.title: Quantum Annealing for Resource Allocation in Next-Generation Wireless Communication Networks: A QUBO Modeling Guide
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.14126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum annealing (QA) offers a physics-inspired approach for such subproblems by mapping them onto an Ising Hamiltonian, which is algebraically equivalent to a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model executable on quantum annealers or hybrid solvers. However, their practical employment in wireless systems critically depends on the specific problem formulation, on the particular variable encoding, constraint handling, solver selection, hardware embedding, and fair benchmarking. This paper develops wireless-oriented QUBO modeling guidelines for QA-assisted resource allocation. We first present a beginner-friendly toy example in which a terrestrial-aerial resource-allocation problem with a fractional signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) maximization objective is reformulated into a two-bit QUBO via Boolean interpolation, converted into an Ising representation, and decoded back into a wireless scheduling decision. The same scheduling is applicable to UAV, aircraft, satellite, and terrestrial links in SAGIN systems. We then review the QA foundations and solver ecosystems, including binary quadratic, discrete quadratic, constrained quadratic, and hybrid models from the perspective of NG wireless optimization. Furthermore, we discuss both binary and discrete encoding, penalty-based constraint conversion, embedding overhead, solution decoding, and feasibility verification. A QUBO Compatibility Index is introduced as a lightweight diagnostic metric for assessing the associated QUBO formulation readiness, rather than a predictor of runtime or solution quality. Finally, a case study on max-min uplink power control in cell-free massive MIMO illustrates how a fairness-oriented wireless problem can be discretized, constrained, converted into the concept of a QUBO, and evaluated against classical baselines. A host of key challenges and future directions are also discussed.
authors: Nguyen Xuan Tung, Le Tung Giang, Mai Dinh Cong, Pham Dang Anh Duc, Nguyen Hoang Viet, Trinh Van Chien, Lajos Hanzo

articles.title: Low-Latency Belief-Propagation Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes with Reinforcement-Learned Scheduling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.15857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Belief propagation (BP) is attractive for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) decoding because of its low complexity and low latency, but short cycles and degeneracy can limit its error-correction performance. Reinforcement-learned sequential scheduling (RL-S) substantially improves this performance by adapting the variable node (VN) update order, although Q-table storage and heap-based selection introduce additional overhead. We propose bucket RL-S (B-RL-S), which quantizes learned Q-values into integer priorities and schedules VN updates using dynamically maintained first-in, first-out buckets. Without retraining or changing the BP message updates, B-RL-S reduces policy storage and refreshes only priorities affected by local residual syndrome changes. A fixed number of priority levels enables constant-time VN selection and queue relocation. For the [[288,12,18]] bivariate bicycle code over the depolarizing channel at p=0.05, B-RL-S with eight priority levels achieves approximately one fifth the block error rate (BLER) of flooding BP followed by order-10 ordered-statistics decoding. The respective caps are 1000 sequential iterations for B-RL-S and 1000 flooding iterations for the BP stage of the reference decoder. These results highlight strong error correction with inexpensive scheduling and no additional post-processing stage.
authors: Mohsen Moradi, Ghilas Aissou, Taejoon Kim, Remi A. Chou, David G. M. Mitchell

articles.title: Symmetric Cryptography via Dirichlet Convolution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.14040v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We discuss a new symmetric-key cipher for digital data encryption. Its implementation is fast, memory efficient, and resilient against classical, AI-assisted, and quantum attacks. Let x, k, and c be elements of a finite abelian group G with operation + and neutral element 0. Suppose one is given ciphertext c=x+k. Retrieving the plaintext x=c-k from the ciphertext is trivial when the key k is known. Without the key, however, recovering x amounts to a blind search. Even if an efficient criterion were available for identifying the plaintext among all group elements, the average number of trials would remain prohibitively large when the group is sufficiently large. The challenge in constructing a practical cryptosystem is therefore to identify a sufficiently rich group G, together with efficient algorithms that enable an immersion of emphreal digital data into G and efficient evaluation of the group operations. The proposed cipher is based on generalized Dirichlet convolution over finite fields. We investigate its security against plaintext attacks from an information-theoretic perspective. The nonlocal structure of Dirichlet convolution naturally permits plaintext salting, providing protection against plaintext attacks while allowing controlled key reuse. We establish perfect masking properties over finite fields and prove that the resulting cipher achieves information-theoretic security under key reuse when the underlying arithmetic is carried out in Fₚ with p>2. For arithmetic over F₂, some information leakage remains, leading to a finite key-reuse budget.
authors: Artur Sowa, Elias Hassani Sangani, Francis Bui, Grant Harris, Jonathan Norton

articles.title: Performance of Planar XYZ and XZZX Codes under Homogeneous and Spatially Nonuniform Noise
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.23236v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) decoder is a standard decoding strategy for surface codes, but its performance can degrade considerably under biased noise. In this work, a modified family of surface codes, termed the XYZ planar code, is introduced, and MWPM is extended to posterior MWPM (pMWPM), which exploits the information provided by mixed stabilizers with almost no increase in decoding complexity. The XYZ--pMWPM and XZZX code--decoder combinations are compared under homogeneous independent and identically distributed (IID) Pauli noise and processor-derived independent nonidentically distributed (INID) noise. Under homogeneous biased Pauli noise, pMWPM substantially increases the threshold of the XYZ planar code relative to conventional MWPM. At finite code distances, particularly for small codes under strong bias, XYZ--pMWPM achieves logical error rates comparable to or lower than those of XZZX. Under INID noise, the pseudothreshold ordering observed under the corresponding homogeneous IID references is not always preserved; in some hardware--distance settings, XYZ--pMWPM achieves pseudothresholds comparable to or higher than those of XZZX. Within XZZX, qubit-specific weighting consistently yields higher INID pseudothresholds than average-rate weighting for the hardware instances considered. It is further found that the IID--INID pseudothreshold shift depends strongly on the physical-error scalarization and the construction of the homogeneous IID reference. These results show that pMWPM efficiently exploits the mixed-stabilizer structure of the XYZ planar code and provides competitive finite-distance decoding under biased and spatially nonuniform noise.
authors: Zhiwei Wang, Liqi Wang

articles.title: Asymptotically good bosonic Fock state codes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.15190v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the error-correction properties of multi-mode Fock-state codes under amplitude-damping (AD) noise, focusing on the asymptotic regime in which the total excitation of the code states grows without limit and the number of photon losses induced by the noise scales linearly with it. In this setting, existing code families, which correct only sublinearly many photon losses, do not protect against amplitude-damping (AD) noise with a constant loss parameter. As our main result, we address this gap by constructing asymptotically good Fock-state codes relying on random classical codes in the discrete simplex. Unlike many standard constructions of random quantum codes, our construction introduces randomness through the underlying classical indexing structure. Randomization also enables another desirable feature: bounded per-mode occupancy, which limits the number of photons in any individual mode and thereby increases the coherence lifetime of the code states. Finally, via a relation between Fock-state codes and permutation-invariant codes, our results also yield asymptotically good families of qudit permutation-invariant codes as well as codes in monolithic nuclear state spaces.
authors: Dor Elimelech, Arda Aydin, Alexander Barg

articles.abstract: Author(s): Yan Lu and Xiao-Feng Shi Although polar molecules are promising candidates for quantum computing, entangling gates built with them suffer from fluctuations in the dipole-dipole interaction (DDI). A high-fidelity molecular gate protocol is introduced that uses an exotic spin echo to suppress population in DDI-active states, alongside a theoretical framework revealing that DDI couples to only half of the motional modes during the gate. articles.title: Probe Signatures of Quantum Chaos with Quantum Sensing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The spectral form factor (SFF), which is the Fourier transform of the two-point spectral correlation, is a fundamental diagnostics of quantum chaos. Nevertheless, its experimental detection in quantum many-body systems was less unexplored until recently. Here, we establish a relationship between the SFF with the quantum Fisher information (QFI) by means of quantum sensing protocols. Furthermore, when the eigenvalues and eigenstates of the disordered Hamiltonian are statistically independent, we prove that QFI is typical both in short and long timescales while numerics suggest that it is also typical at intermediate timescales, which ensures self-averaging of QFI. The self-averaging property renders the experimental measurement of QFI with our protocol less noisy in contrast with the direct measurement of SFF which is known to be non-self-averaging. Our results reveal an intriguing connection between quantum noise and the signatures of quantum chaos.
authors: Isaías Vallejo-Fabila, Jing Yang

articles.title: Quantum Walks on Arbitrary Spatial Networks with Rydberg Atoms

articles.abstract: Quantum 10, 2235 (2026). https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-10-13-2235 Rydberg atoms provide a highly promising platform for quantum computation, leveraging their strong tunable interactions to encode and manipulate information in the electronic states of individual atoms. Key advantages of Rydberg atoms include scalability, reconfigurable connectivity, and native multi-qubit gates, making them particularly well-suited for addressing complex network problems. These problems can often be framed as graph-based tasks, which can be efficiently addressed using quantum walks. In this work, we propose a general implementation of staggered quantum walks with Rydberg atoms, with a particular focus on spatial networks. We also present an efficient algorithm for constructing the tessellations required for the staggered quantum walk. Finally, we demonstrate that our proposal achieves performance consistent with a quadratic speedup in spatial search algorithms.
articles.abstract_zh: 里德堡原子是量子计算的理想平台，可用于解决复杂的网络问题。本文提出了一种利用里德堡原子实现交错量子行走的通用方法，特别关注空间网络。研究还提供了一种构建交错量子行走所需镶嵌的高效算法，并展示了该方案在空间搜索算法中实现了二次加速。

articles.title: Sampled-Based Guided Quantum Walk: Non-variational quantum algorithm for combinatorial optimization
articles.title_zh: 基于采样的引导量子行走：用于组合优化的非变分量子算法
articles.abstract: Quantum 10, 2234 (2026). https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-10-13-2234 We introduce SamBa-GQW, a novel quantum algorithm for solving binary combinatorial optimization problems of arbitrary degree with no use of any classical optimizer. The algorithm is based on a continuous-time quantum walk on the solution space represented as a graph. The walker explores the solution space to find its way to vertices that minimize the cost function of the optimization problem. The key novelty of our algorithm is an offline classical sampling protocol that gives information about the spectrum of the problem Hamiltonian. Then, the extracted information is used to guide the walker to high quality solutions via a quantum walk with a time-dependent hopping rate. We investigate the performance of SamBa-GQW on several quadratic problems, namely MaxCut, maximum independent set, portfolio optimization, and higher-order polynomial problems such as LABS, MAX-k-SAT and a quartic reformulation of the travelling salesperson problem. We empirically demonstrate that SamBa-GQW finds high quality approximate solutions on problems up to a size of n=30 qubits by only sampling poly(n) states among 2ⁿ possible decisions. Furthermore, SamBa-GQW compares in par with classically optimized variational approaches, such as the variational guided quantum walk and QAOA (the latter when run on deep circuits). This places Samba-GQW as a promising heuristic to tackle combinatorial problems beyond the NISQ regime.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文提出了一种名为SamBa-GQW的新型量子算法，用于解决任意度数的二元组合优化问题，无需经典优化器。该算法基于解空间上的连续时间量子行走，并通过离线经典采样协议获取问题哈密顿量的谱信息，从而引导量子行走器找到高质量的解。实验证明，SamBa-GQW能在多达30个量子比特的问题上找到高质量的近似解。

articles.title: Exact solutions of non-Markovian dissipative Ising models
articles.title_zh: 非马尔可夫耗散伊辛模型的精确解
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Applications of quantum devices and simulators require an accurate understanding of their dynamics as well as the effects of environmental noise. While some sources of noise can be modeled as Markovian dissipation, coupling to resonators or vibrational modes often produces non-Markovian dynamics as well, making it difficult to characterize the system, particularly for interacting many-body systems. Here, we identify a broad class of exactly solvable many-body quantum systems with both non-Markovian dynamics and Markovian dissipation. We consider a prototypical model of spins coupled to lossy bosonic modes that mediate Ising-type interactions. We exclude a transverse field but allow local spin dissipation that need not commute with the interactions, including dephasing, relaxation, pumping, and even processes that generate coherences. Using an exact stochastic representation, we decouple the many-body dynamics into the evolution of individual spins, yielding exact spin observables and correlations without adiabatically eliminating the bosons. In the Markovian limit, our solutions describe Ising models with correlated dephasing and nonreciprocal interactions. An example of spin squeezing shows that both the achievable squeezing and its optimal preparation time depend strongly on the interplay between non-Markovian dynamics and Markovian dissipation.
articles.abstract_zh: 量子设备和模拟器的应用需要准确理解其动力学及环境噪声的影响。本文识别出一类具有非马尔可夫动力学和马尔可夫耗散的精确可解多体量子系统。通过使用精确的随机表示，研究人员将多体动力学解耦为单个自旋的演化，从而获得了精确的自旋可观测量和关联。在马尔可夫极限下，这些解描述了具有相关退相干的伊辛模型。
authors: Mohammad Maghrebi

articles.title: Engineering Ergodicity-Breaking and Stable Emergent Conservation Laws in a Generic Quantum Many-body System Under Strong Periodic Drive
articles.title_zh: 在强周期驱动下通用量子多体系统中设计遍历性破缺和稳定的涌现守恒定律
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A periodically driven quantum many-body system is believed to approach a locally infinite-temperature-like state as dictated by the ergodicity hypothesis, when all the couplings/parameters are of the same order. When the drive is stronger than a threshold value, a large class of systems is shown to break this mandate, exhibiting Dynamical Freezing (DF): ergodicity is broken due to the emergence of local operators with permanent memory of their initial values (PRX 11, 021008, 2021). However, an exception to DF has recently been noted in a particular setting (PRX 16, 011041, 2026). Here we identify the condition for ergodicity-breaking in a system under strong drive, and show how to stabilize DF by exact, local engineering. We further show that the Floquet Hamiltonian Hₑff = (i/T)łn[U(T)] is non-local when ordered by spin-flips, in a non-DF system, while it turns quasi-local under our simple, local DF engineering that keeps the Hamiltonian H(t) still non-integrable at each t. This perplexing non-universality is absent in equilibrium, where non-integrability is believed to imply ergodicity and thermalization universally. Our work paves a way to engineering novel ergodicity-broken interacting Floquet phases of matter in various quantum platforms, and also endows DF-assisted quantum error mitigation and state stabilization techniques (see Nature 653, 1027 (2026)) with unprecedented versatility and flexibility.
articles.abstract_zh: 周期性驱动的量子多体系统通常被认为会趋于局部无限温度态，但当驱动强度超过阈值时，许多系统会表现出动力学冻结（DF），即遍历性破缺。本文确定了强驱动下系统遍历性破缺的条件，并展示了如何通过精确的局部工程来稳定动力学冻结。研究发现，在非DF系统中，Floquet哈密顿量是非局域的，但在局部DF工程下变为准局域，这揭示了非平衡态中非普适性的存在。
authors: Sagnik Chaudhuri, Anirban Das, Asmi Haldar, Arnab Das

articles.title: Error correction and quantum information spreading on sparse random graphs
articles.title_zh: 稀疏随机图上的纠错与量子信息传播
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum error-correcting codes on graph geometries beyond regular euclidean lattices have emerged as a promising route toward robust quantum information processing. A major challenge in quantum error correction is the trade-off between favorable properties of codes constructed in high dimensionality and the need for locality in practical implementations on near-term hardware. Sparse intermediate geometries may combine the advantages of both, but how their structure governs quantum information dynamics and code performance remains unclear. Here we show that the spectral dimension dₛ, defined from the low-energy spectrum of the graph Laplacian, is the universal parameter connecting these properties. Using Floquet random Clifford circuits on two distinct sparse graph architectures with tunable spectral dimension, we find that dₛ governs both quantum information spreading and the scaling of the resulting quantum error-correcting code distance. We identify a geometry-induced entanglement phase transition from localized area-law to ergodic volume-law, whose universality is determined by dₛ and exhibits long-range percolation criticality. In the ergodic phase, the circuit acts as a CSS code encoder whose code distance is set by the competition between two logical sectors --- the cost of severing the graph and the length of its shortest winding cycle --- which connectivity pushes in opposite directions. The spectral dimension organizes this trade-off, highlighting a maximum at intermediate dₛ retaining sparse connectivity and physical realizability.
articles.abstract_zh: 量子纠错码在非欧几里得图几何上的应用为鲁棒量子信息处理提供了新途径。本文研究了稀疏随机图上量子信息动力学和纠错码性能，发现图拉普拉斯算子的低能谱定义的谱维度 dₛ 是连接这些性质的普适参数。研究表明，dₛ 控制着量子信息传播和纠错码距离的标度，并识别出一种由几何引起的纠缠相变。
authors: Giovanni Cemin, Marin Bukov, Andrea Solfanelli

articles.title: Analog quantum simulation of Shastry-Sutherland Ising materials
articles.title_zh: Shastry-Sutherland伊辛材料的模拟量子模拟
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frustrated magnets host rich emergent behavior because competing interactions generate dense manifolds of low-energy states. The Ising Shastry-Sutherland model is a paradigmatic setting, motivated experimentally by Ising-like rare-earth tetraborides such as TmB₄ and ErB₄, whose field-induced magnetization plateaus have motivated extensive microscopic modeling. Yet how tunable quantum fluctuations reorganize this material-motivated phase diagram remains largely unexplored. Here, we realize a transverse- and longitudinal-field Ising model on the Shastry-Sutherland lattice using a programmable Rydberg-atom array. We map its quantum phase diagram using density matrix renormalization group calculations and probe corresponding signatures experimentally in arrays containing more than 110 atoms. Beyond the established classical phases, the calculations identify two regimes absent in the classical limit and stabilized at finite transverse field: a 2/5 filling plateau whose finite stability region emerges from a classically degenerate phase boundary and a symmetry-preserving quantum-dimer regime replacing classically selected collinear order. Experiments on finite open arrays reveal signatures consistent with these regimes across three boundary-pinning conditions, with the resulting response maps agreeing qualitatively with the calculated phase diagram. Our results establish programmable Rydberg-atom arrays as tools for exploring frustrated, material-motivated Hamiltonians and motivate searches for new, quantum-driven magnetization plateaus and quantum-dimer behavior in ErB₄ under a transverse field or in strain-tuned TmB₄.
articles.abstract_zh: 阻挫磁体因竞争相互作用而产生丰富的涌现行为。本文利用可编程里德堡原子阵列，在Shastry-Sutherland晶格上实现了横向和纵向场伊辛模型。通过密度矩阵重整化群计算和实验探测，研究人员绘制了其量子相图。结果揭示了在有限横向场下稳定的两个新量子态：一个2/5填充平台和一个对称保持的量子二聚体态，这些在经典极限下是不存在的。
authors: Vahagn Mkhitaryan, Milan Kornjača, Mao Lin, Alexander Schuckert, Majd Hamdan, Sergio H. Cantú, Ammar Ali, Tommaso Macrí, Nathan Gemelke, Alexander Keesling, Peter Komar, Travis S.
